payload.name: Preserve Distinct Prior Plans on Update
payload.description: When updating or merging an existing memory with a new plan or event, use if the new evidence involves a different activity, date, or companion than the stored memory.
content: During CRUD, before UPDATE or MERGE of an existing memory, compare the new plan's activity, participants, and timing with the stored memory's existing facets.

If the new plan is a different activity or a separate scheduled occurrence (e.g., painting next Saturday vs. kayaking on a later date), do not overwrite the existing memory content; create a new memory for the new plan or merge only the new distinct facets while preserving the old plan and its date.
Treat evidence as contradictory only when it explicitly denies or replaces the exact same planned activity and time; otherwise preserve the prior fact.
Stop after storing the new plan once; do not create near-duplicate memories of the same plan.

solves: Construction agents sometimes overwrite a previously stored plan or event memory when a later, unrelated plan is mentioned, discarding the original fact. This skill ensures distinct plans with different activities, dates, or participants are kept as separate memories, and prior facts are preserved unless new evidence directly contradicts them.
